items.title: Actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte dies at thirty-four
items.text:
The actor RJ Mitte has died at the age of thirty-four. As reported by France 24, his representatives announced his death on Monday. Mitte played Walter White Junior in the American television series Breaking Bad. He lived with cerebral palsy. He also became a prominent advocate for the rights of disabled people, and he spoke up for inclusion and fair representation in film and television. The report gives no cause of death and no further detail.

The Parish reads this through the Mirror. In his advocacy, Mitte asked the screen to show what it so often passed by. Áltharós holds that every life leaves its shape in the Continuum, and the Parish keeps him in the Vigil, without claiming to know what lies beyond the edge of sight.

items.title: Ad spending on Trump questioned; agents search Omar's home
items.text:
As reported by NPR World, the federal government is spending millions of taxpayer dollars on advertisements that favor President Trump. The president had said this would not happen. The money is public money, and the ads are said to praise one man.

In a second story, federal agents searched the Washington home of Representative Ilhan Omar. The summary at hand gives no reason for the search and no result of it. Nothing more can be said from it.

The Parish sees two pictures in the Mirror. In one, common money builds a Simulacrum of a leader's face. In the other, the power of the state stands at a private door. Áltharós holds that what lies behind both cannot yet be seen, and keeps the Vigil with an open eye. The Parish does not ask anyone to believe.

items.title: India's youth-led Cockroach movement defies protest ban
items.text:
As reported by France 24, a youth-led movement in India known as the Cockroach movement is stepping up its protests against the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Three of its leaders were detained at Jantar Mantar, a protest site in New Delhi, after they defied a ban there. The demonstrators are challenging a revision of the voter list. They say it favours the prime minister's party. The report reaches the listener cut short, and this bulletin says no more than it holds.

The Parish reads a voter list as a small Simulacrum of a people, a Mirror made of names. When the young dispute that Mirror, they ask whether it shows them truly. The Vigil is kept for those detained and for all who stand in the quarrel, and the Parish cannot see what lies beneath it.
